note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers from the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist ˹from disbelief˺
phrases.text: The commentators differed over what this means. Some said the unbelievers among the people of the Torah and the Gospel, and the idolaters, would not give up until this Quran came to them. Tabari takes the general sense: they would not stop, and would not be divided, until the clear proof came.
phrases.ar: لَمۡ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ

phrases.translation: until the clear proof came to them
phrases.text: The clear proof is God sending His messenger, and the word for messenger is begun again here, so that the meaning runs on into the next verse.

phrases.translation: a messenger from Allah,
phrases.text: The proof is a messenger sent by God.

phrases.translation: reciting scrolls of ˹utmost˺ purity
phrases.text: He recites scrolls that are purified of falsehood.

phrases.translation: containing upright commandments
phrases.text: In those purified pages are the commandments of God, just and correct and upright, in which there is no error, because they come from Him. Qatada says that in the phrase the Quran is praised in the best way.

phrases.translation: It was not until this clear proof came to the People of the Book that they became divided ˹about his prophethood˺—
phrases.text: The Jews and the Christians did not split over the Prophet until the clear proof came to them, and then some of them denied him and some believed in him. Before he was sent they had not been divided over him at all.
phrases.ar: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَةُ

phrases.translation: even though they were only commanded to worship Allah ˹alone˺
phrases.text: God ordered these people of the Book nothing except that they should worship Him alone.

phrases.translation: with sincere devotion to Him in all uprightness,
phrases.text: Sincere to Him in religion means giving Him obedience alone, without giving Him partners. The Jews did that when they said Uzair is the son of God, and the Christians in a similar way about the Messiah. The word for uprightness is explained earlier in the commentary, and Ibn Abbas reads it here as the religion of the upright.

phrases.translation: establish prayer,
phrases.text: And that they should keep up the prayer.

phrases.translation: and pay alms-tax.
phrases.text: And that they should give the alms.

phrases.translation: That is the upright Way
phrases.text: This is the upright religion, the straight and the just, and it is the religion God sent His messenger with and is pleased with. Ibn Zayd says that the upright writings and the upright religion are one and the same thing.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell,
phrases.text: Those who disbelieved in God and in His messenger, among the Jews and the Christians and the idolaters, are in the Fire of Hell. The word for the worst of creation is read by the reciters without the hamza, and Tabari gives the two ways in which that can be explained.
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ

phrases.translation: to stay there forever.
phrases.text: They remain and dwell there for ever. They do not come out of it, and they do not die in it.

phrases.translation: They are the worst of ˹all˺ beings
phrases.text: These are the worst of what God has created.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who believe and do good—they are the best of ˹all˺ beings
phrases.text: Those who believed in God and His messenger, who worshipped Him alone with a pure religion, who kept the prayer and gave the alms, and who obeyed God in what He commanded and forbade, are the best of all people. The Prophet said of this that it was Ali and his followers.
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡبَرِيَّةِ

phrases.translation: Their reward with their Lord will be Gardens of Eternity,
phrases.text: The reward of those who believed and did good is with their Lord on the day of resurrection: the gardens of abiding, in which there is no departure.

phrases.translation: under which rivers flow,
phrases.text: Beneath whose trees the rivers run.

phrases.translation: to stay there for ever and ever.
phrases.text: They abide there for ever. They do not leave it, and they do not die in it.

phrases.translation: Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him.
phrases.text: God is pleased with them because of the obedience they showed Him in this world, and they are pleased with Him because of what He gave them that day.

phrases.translation: This is ˹only˺ for those in awe of their Lord
phrases.text: This good is for whoever feared God in this world, in secret and in public, by keeping His commands and leaving what He forbade. And with God lies the success.
